title.zh: 卷一百四十 列傳第二十七: 別兒怯不花 太平 鐵木兒塔識 達識帖睦邇
title.en: Volume 140 Biographies 27: Bie'erqiebuhua, Taiping, Tiemuertashi, Dashitiemuer
title.raw: 卷一百四十 列傳第二十七: 別兒怯不花 太平 鐵木兒塔識 達識帖睦邇 Volume 140 Biographies 27: Bie'erqiebuhua, Taiping, Tiemuertashi, Dashitiemuer

sentences.zh: 別兒怯不花

translations.literal: Bie'erqiebuhua
translations.idiomatic: Bie'erqiebuhua

sentences.zh: 別兒怯不花，字大用，燕只吉氏。

translations.literal: Bie'erqiebuhua, whose courtesy name was Dayong, was of the Yanzhijias clan.
translations.idiomatic: Bie'erqiebuhua, styled Dayong, belonged to the Yanzhijias clan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖忙怯禿以千戶從憲宗南征有功。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Mangqiatu, as a commander of a thousand households, followed Emperor Xianzong on the southern campaign and rendered meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Mangqiatu had served as a chiliarch on Emperor Xianzong's southern campaign and won distinction.

sentences.zh: 父阿忽台事成宗為丞相，被誅，後贈和寧忠獻王。

translations.literal: His father Ahuotai served Emperor Chengzong as grand councillor and was executed; he was later enfeoffed posthumously as Prince Heining, with the posthumous title Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ahuotai had been grand councillor under Emperor Chengzong and was put to death; afterward he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Heining, with the temple name Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 別兒怯不花蚤孤，八歲，以興聖太后及武宗命，侍明宗於籓邸。

translations.literal: Bie'erqiebuhua lost his father early; at eight, by order of Empress Dowager Xingsheng and Emperor Wuzong, he attended Emperor Mingzong at the princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, at the age of eight Bie'erqiebuhua was placed, on the orders of Empress Dowager Xingsheng and Emperor Wuzong, in attendance on Emperor Mingzong at his fief.

sentences.zh: 尋入國子學為諸生。

translations.literal: Soon he entered the Imperial Academy as a student.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered the Imperial Academy as a student.

sentences.zh: 會明宗以周王出鎮雲南，別兒怯不花從行，至大同而還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong went out as Prince of Zhou to garrison Yunnan, Bie'erqiebuhua accompanied him and returned when they reached Datong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong was sent to garrison Yunnan as Prince of Zhou, Bie'erqiebuhua went with him and turned back at Datong.

sentences.zh: 仁宗召入宿衛。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong summoned him into the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong summoned him into the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 一日，從殿中望見其儀榘夐異，即召對，慰諭之。

translations.literal: One day, looking from the hall he saw Bie'erqiebuhua's bearing and deportment markedly unusual and immediately summoned him for an audience and spoke words of comfort and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor, gazing from the hall, noticed his bearing and deportment were strikingly out of the ordinary and summoned him at once for an audience and words of encouragement.

sentences.zh: 八番宣撫司長乃其世職，英宗遂授懷遠大將軍、八番宣撫司達魯花赤。

translations.literal: The post of director of the Baban Pacification Commission had been a hereditary office in his family; Emperor Yingzong therefore appointed him Huaiyuan General and darughachi of the Baban Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The directorship of the Baban Pacification Commission was a hereditary office of his line, and Emperor Yingzong accordingly appointed him Huaiyuan General and darughachi of that commission.

sentences.zh: 既至，宣布國家恩信，峒民感悅。

translations.literal: Once he had arrived, he proclaimed the state's grace and good faith, and the cave-dwelling peoples were moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: After he took up the post, he proclaimed the dynasty's grace and trust, and the cave peoples were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 有累歲不服者，皆喜曰：「吾故賢帥子孫也，其敢違命。」

translations.literal: Those who had refused submission for many years all rejoiced, saying, "He is the worthy scion of our old commandant — who would dare defy his command."
translations.idiomatic: Tribes that had withheld submission for years now exclaimed joyfully, "Surely he is the worthy descendant of our former commander — who would dare disobey."

sentences.zh: 率其十四部來受約束。

translations.literal: They led their fourteen divisions to come and accept his rule.
translations.idiomatic: They led forth their fourteen divisions to submit to his authority.

sentences.zh: 別兒怯不花以其事入奏，天子嘉而留之。

translations.literal: Bie'erqiebuhua memorialized this to the throne; the Son of Heaven approved and kept him at court.
translations.idiomatic: Bie'erqiebuhua reported this to the throne; the emperor commended him and kept him at court.

sentences.zh: 泰定三年，特授同知太常禮儀院事，益從耆老文學之士雍容議論。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiding, he was specially appointed associate director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and increasingly joined aged elders and men of letters in unhurried discussion.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiding he was given a special appointment as associate director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and increasingly took part in easy discourse with elders and literary men.

sentences.zh: 尋拜監察御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷中書右司郎中。

translations.literal: The following year he was transferred to right section director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred to right section director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又明年，升參議中書省事。

translations.literal: The year after that he was promoted to associate administrator of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he rose to associate administrator of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 居二年，除吏部尚書。

translations.literal: After two years he was made Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，其兄治書侍御史自當諫止明里董阿子閭閭不當為監察御史，並出別兒怯不花為廣西兩江道宣慰使司都元帥。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun, his elder brother the supervising censor Zidang remonstrated that Mingli Dong'a's son Lü Lübu should not serve as investigating censor; Bie'erqiebuhua was also dismissed and made commander-in-chief of the Guangxi Liangjiang Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhishun his elder brother Zidang, in his capacity as supervising censor, objected that Mingli Dong'a's son Lü Lübu ought not hold an investigatorial post; Bie'erqiebuhua too was dismissed and appointed commander-in-chief of the Guangxi Liangjiang Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 未幾，丁內艱還京。

translations.literal: Before long he returned to the capital on bereavement leave for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he returned to the capital to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 起復為江浙行省參知政事。

translations.literal: He was recalled from mourning to serve as associate administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled from mourning to serve as associate administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 江浙歲漕米由海道達京師，別兒怯不花董其事。

translations.literal: Each year the Jiang-Zhe region transported tax grain to the capital by sea route; Bie'erqiebuhua oversaw this affair.
translations.idiomatic: Each year Jiang-Zhe's tax rice reached the capital by sea; Bie'erqiebuhua directed the operation.

sentences.zh: 尋除禮部尚書，遷徽政院副使，擢侍御史，特命領宿衛，升榮祿大夫、宣徽使，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Minister of Rites, transferred to vice director of the Xuanzhen Court, promoted to palace censor, specially ordered to lead the palace guard, elevated to Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, made Xuanzhen Commissioner, and granted the privilege of Opening the Government with the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Minister of Rites, then vice director of the Xuanzhen Court, then palace censor, with a special order to head the palace guard; he was raised to Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, made Xuanzhen Commissioner, and granted Privileges Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 凡宿衛士有從掌領官薦用者，往往所舉多其親暱。

translations.literal: Whenever palace guards were recommended for appointment by their supervising officers, those recommended were often the officers' own kin and intimates.
translations.idiomatic: When palace guards were advanced on the recommendation of their supervising officers, the nominees were often those officers' kin and favorites.

sentences.zh: 至別兒怯不花獨推擇歲久者舉之，眾論翕服。

translations.literal: Only Bie'erqiebuhua selected men of long service for recommendation, and popular opinion was entirely persuaded.
translations.idiomatic: Bie'erqiebuhua alone put forward men of long service, and opinion among the guards was unanimous in his favor.

sentences.zh: 宣徽所造酒，橫索者眾，歲費陶瓶甚多。

translations.literal: The wine made by the Xuanzhen Office attracted many who demanded it by extortion, and each year a great quantity of pottery bottles was consumed.
translations.idiomatic: Wine from the Xuanzhen Office drew many extortionate demands, costing a vast number of pottery bottles every year.

sentences.zh: 別兒怯不怯花奏制銀瓶以貯，而索者遂止。

translations.literal: Bie'erqiebuhua memorialized that silver bottles should be made for storage, and the extortionists then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Bie'erqiebuhua memorialized that silver bottles be used for storage, and the extortion then stopped.

sentences.zh: 至元四年，拜御史大夫、知經筵事，尋遷中書平章。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhizheng he was made Censor-in-Chief and director of the Classics Collegium; soon he was transferred to Central Secretariat Vice Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhizheng he became Censor-in-Chief and overseer of the Classics Collegium, and was soon transferred to vice councilor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至正二年，拜江浙行省左丞相。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizheng he was made Left Councilor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhizheng he was appointed Left Councilor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 行至淮東，聞杭城大火燒官廨民廬幾盡，仰天揮涕曰：「杭，浙省所治，吾被命出鎮，而火如此，是我不德累杭人也。」

translations.literal: When he reached the Huai River region, he heard that in Hangzhou a great fire had burned government offices and private dwellings almost entirely; he lifted his face to heaven and wiped away tears, saying, "Hangzhou is where the Jiang-Zhe Province is seated; I have been ordered to go out and govern there — that such a fire should break out means my lack of virtue has brought calamity upon the people of Hang."
translations.idiomatic: En route on the Huai River east he learned that a great fire in Hangzhou had burned away nearly all government offices and private homes. He looked heavenward in tears and said, "Hang is the seat of Jiang-Zhe Province; I have been sent to govern it — that fire like this means my own want of virtue has visited woe on Hang's people."

sentences.zh: 疾馳赴鎮，即下令錄被災者二萬三千餘戶，戶給鈔一錠，焚死者亦如之，人給月米二斗，幼稚給其半。

translations.literal: He galloped swiftly to his post, immediately ordered a register of more than twenty-three thousand disaster-stricken households, and gave each household one ingot of paper money; those burned to death were treated the same; each person was given two dou of rice per month, and children half that amount.
translations.idiomatic: He galloped to his post at once, registered more than twenty-three thousand stricken households, and gave each household one ingot of paper money, with the same for those who had perished in the flames; each person received two dou of rice a month, and children half as much.

sentences.zh: 又請日減酒課，為錢千二百五十緡，織坊減元額之半，軍器、漆器權停一年，泛稅皆停。

translations.literal: He also requested a daily reduction of the wine tax by 1,250 strings of cash, a halving of the weaving workshops' original quotas, a temporary suspension for one year of arms and lacquerware levies, and a halt to all miscellaneous taxes.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned to cut the wine tax by 1,250 strings of cash per day, halve the weaving workshops' original quotas, suspend arms and lacquerware levies for a year, and halt all miscellaneous taxes.

sentences.zh: 事聞，朝廷從之。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the court approved.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, it approved his requests.

sentences.zh: 又大作省治，民居附其旁者，增直買其基，募民就役，則厚其傭直。

translations.literal: He also undertook a major rebuilding of the provincial offices; for dwellings adjoining the site he paid premium prices to buy their foundations, and when recruiting the people for labor he gave generous wages.
translations.idiomatic: He also rebuilt the provincial compound on a large scale, buying out adjoining homes at premium prices and paying generous wages to those he recruited for the work.

sentences.zh: 又請歲減江浙、福建鹽課十三萬引。

translations.literal: He also requested an annual reduction of 130,000 yin of the salt tax in Jiang-Zhe and Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned to reduce the annual salt levy in Jiang-Zhe and Fujian by 130,000 yin.

sentences.zh: 或遇淫雨亢旱，輒出禱於神祠，所禱無不應。

translations.literal: Whenever there was excessive rain or severe drought, he would go out to pray at spirit shrines, and his prayers were invariably answered.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever floods or drought struck, he went out to pray at local shrines, and his prayers were invariably answered.

sentences.zh: 在鎮二年，雖兒童女婦莫不感其恩。

translations.literal: During his two years in the post, even children and women were moved by his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: In two years at his post, even children and women felt the warmth of his rule.

sentences.zh: 召還，除翰林學士承旨，仍掌宿衛。

translations.literal: He was recalled and made Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy, while still directing the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was made Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy while continuing to head the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜中書左丞相。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made Left Councilor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed Left Councilor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 朝廷議選奉使宣撫，使問民疾苦，察吏貪廉，且選習北籓風土及知典故者，俾別兒怯不花周行沙漠，洗冤除弊，不可勝計。

translations.literal: The court deliberated on selecting commissioners for pacification tours to inquire into the people's hardships and examine officials' corruption and integrity; choosing one versed in the customs of the northern fiefs and knowledgeable in precedent, they sent Bie'erqiebuhua to travel throughout the desert regions, redressing wrongs and removing abuses beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The court chose commissioners to tour the realm, hear the people's grievances, and scrutinize officials for corruption; Bie'erqiebuhua, versed in northern frontier customs and court precedent, was sent to travel the desert regions and redressed wrongs and abuses beyond number.

sentences.zh: 又奏發使諭諸王，賜以金衣重寶，使各撫其民，毋逾法制，於是內外震肅。

translations.literal: He also memorialized dispatching envoys to instruct the princes, bestowing on them golden robes and heavy treasures, and ordering each to cherish his people and not transgress the laws; thereby court and countryside were awed into order.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized sending envoys to instruct the princes, gifting them golden robes and rich treasures, and charging each to care for his people and keep within the law; court and countryside were awed into order.

sentences.zh: 明年，歲大饑，流民載道，令有司賑之，欲還鄉者給路糧。

translations.literal: The following year there was a great famine; refugees filled the roads; he ordered the authorities to provide relief, and those wishing to return home were given travel rations.
translations.idiomatic: The next year famine struck; refugees thronged the roads; he ordered officials to provide relief and gave travel rations to those who wished to return home.

sentences.zh: 又錄在京貧民，日糶以糧。

translations.literal: He also registered the poor of the capital and sold them grain daily at reduced price.
translations.idiomatic: He also registered the capital's poor and sold them grain daily at reduced prices.

sentences.zh: 帝還自上都，遣中使數輩趣使迎謁，比見，帝親酌酒勞之。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned from Shangdu, he sent several palace envoys urging Bie'erqiebuhua to come and pay his respects; when they met, the emperor personally poured wine to reward him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from Shangdu, he sent several palace envoys urging Bie'erqiebuhua to come and pay his respects; at their meeting the emperor personally poured wine to honor him.

sentences.zh: 七年，進右丞相。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to Right Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted to Right Councilor.

sentences.zh: 明年，御史劾奏別兒怯不花，而徽政院使高龍卜在帝側為解，帝遂不允。

translations.literal: The following year the censors memorialized impeaching Bie'erqiebuhua, but Xuanzhen Commissioner Gaolongbu spoke in his defense at the emperor's side, and the emperor would not approve.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the censors impeached Bie'erqiebuhua, but Xuanzhen Commissioner Gaolongbu pleaded his case at the emperor's side, and the throne would not assent.

sentences.zh: 乃出御史大夫亦憐真班為江浙左丞相，中丞以下皆辭職。

translations.literal: Bie'erqiebuhua was then dismissed and Censor-in-Chief Yilianzhenban made Left Councilor of Jiang-Zhe; the vice censor-in-chief and those below all resigned their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Bie'erqiebuhua was dismissed and Censor-in-Chief Yilianzhenban sent out as Left Councilor of Jiang-Zhe; the vice censor-in-chief and his subordinates all resigned in protest.

sentences.zh: 詔復加太保。

translations.literal: An edict again added to his title Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored to him the rank of Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 於是兩台各道言章交至，別兒怯不花益不自安，尋謫居渤海縣。

translations.literal: Thereupon memorials from both censorates and every circuit arrived in succession; Bie'erqiebuhua grew ever more ill at ease and was soon demoted to residence in Bohai County.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials from both censorates and every circuit then poured in; Bie'erqiebuhua grew ever more uneasy and was soon banished to Bohai County.

sentences.zh: 十年正月卒。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of the tenth year.

sentences.zh: 後子達世帖木而用於朝，遂贈弘仁輔治秉文守正寅亮同德功臣、開府儀同三司、上柱國、太師，追封冀王，諡忠宣。

translations.literal: Later, when his son Dashitiemuer was employed at court, he was posthumously granted the title of meritorious minister Hongren Fuzhi Bingwen Shouzheng Yinliang Tongde, Privileges Equal to the Three Excellencies, Pillar of the State, and Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Ji, with the posthumous title Zhongxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his son Dashitiemuer came into service at court, Bie'erqiebuhua was posthumously granted the title of meritorious minister Hongren Fuzhi Bingwen Shouzheng Yinliang Tongde, Privileges Equal to the Three Excellencies, Pillar of the State, and Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Ji, with the temple name Zhongxuan.

sentences.zh: 達世帖木而字原理，仕至中書平章政事，有學識，能世其家。

translations.literal: Dashitiemuer, courtesy name Yuanli, rose to Central Secretariat Vice Councilor; he was learned and able to carry on his family's tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Dashitiemuer, styled Yuanli, rose to vice councilor of the Central Secretariat; learned and able, he upheld his family's reputation.

sentences.zh: 太平，字允中，初姓賀氏，名惟一，後賜姓蒙古氏，名太平，仁傑之孫，勝之子也。

translations.literal: Taiping, courtesy name Yunzhong, was originally surnamed He and named Weiyi; later he was granted the Mongol surname and the name Taiping; he was the grandson of Renjie and the son of Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping, styled Yunzhong, was born He Weiyi of the He clan; later he was granted the Mongol surname and the name Taiping. He was the grandson of Renjie and the son of Sheng.

sentences.zh: 初，勝以非罪死，太平年尚幼，泰定帝雪其父冤而撫卹之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Sheng had died for a crime he did not commit; Taiping was still young; Emperor Taiding cleared his father's name and nurtured and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng had earlier been put to death on a false charge when Taiping was still a boy; Emperor Taiding cleared his father's name and raised him with care.

sentences.zh: 太平資性開朗正大，雖在弱齡，儼然如老成人。

translations.literal: Taiping's nature was open, bright, and upright; though still in his youth, he was as grave as a seasoned adult.
translations.idiomatic: Open and upright by nature, Taiping carried himself with the gravity of a seasoned man even in youth.

sentences.zh: 嘗受業於趙孟頫，又師事雲中呂弼。

translations.literal: He had studied under Zhao Mengfu and also took as his teacher Lü Bi of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He had studied under Zhao Mengfu and also took Lü Bi of Yunzhong as his teacher.

sentences.zh: 太平始襲父職，為虎賁親軍都指揮使，尋擢陝西漢中道廉訪副使。

translations.literal: Taiping first inherited his father's post as commander-in-chief of the Huben Imperial Guard, and was soon promoted to vice surveillance commissioner of the Shaanxi Hanzhong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping first inherited his father's post as commander-in-chief of the Huben Imperial Guard and was soon promoted to vice surveillance commissioner of the Shaanxi Hanzhong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 文宗召為工部尚書，都主管奎章閣工事，又除上都留守同知。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong summoned him as Minister of Works and superintendent of Kuizhang Pavilion construction, and also made him associate intendant of Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong summoned him as Minister of Works and superintendent of Kuizhang Pavilion construction, and also appointed him associate intendant of Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 順帝元統初，命為樞密副使，尋升同知樞密院事，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuantong under Emperor Shundi, he was appointed vice commissioner of the Privy Council; soon he was promoted to associate commissioner of the Privy Council and transferred to vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yuantong era under Emperor Shundi he was made vice commissioner of the Privy Council, soon rose to associate commissioner, and was transferred to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時中書有參議佛家閭者，憸人也。

translations.literal: At that time among the Central Secretariat associate administrators was one Fojialü, a treacherous man.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Central Secretariat had an associate administrator named Fojialü, a treacherous man.

sentences.zh: 御史劾其罪，時宰庇之，事寢不行。

translations.literal: The censors impeached him for his crimes, but the chief ministers sheltered him and the matter was shelved and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The censors impeached him, but the chief ministers shielded him and the case was quietly dropped.

sentences.zh: 太平辭疾臥家。

translations.literal: Taiping pleaded illness and remained at home in bed.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping pleaded illness and retired to his home.

sentences.zh: 至正二年，詔起為中書參知政事，辭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizheng an edict recalled him as associate administrator of the Central Secretariat; he declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhizheng an edict recalled him as associate administrator of the Central Secretariat; he declined.

sentences.zh: 進右丞，又辭。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Vice Councilor and again declined.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Right Vice Councilor, he declined again.

sentences.zh: 會御史祁君璧复劾佛家閭，黜之，乃起就職。

translations.literal: When investigating censor Qi Junbi again impeached Fojialü and he was dismissed, Taiping then rose and took up his post.
translations.idiomatic: When investigating censor Qi Junbi impeached Fojialü again and he was dismissed, Taiping at last accepted office.

sentences.zh: 宗室諸王歲賜廩食衣幣不均，太平請於帝，均其厚薄。

translations.literal: The annual grants of grain, clothing, and silks to the imperial clan princes were uneven; Taiping petitioned the emperor to equalize their amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Annual grants of grain, clothing, and silks to the imperial princes were uneven; Taiping petitioned the emperor to equalize them.

sentences.zh: 守令多失職，請選臺閣名臣充之。

translations.literal: Many prefects and magistrates were derelict in duty; he requested that renowned ministers from the censorate and secretariat be selected to fill these posts.
translations.idiomatic: Many local officials were failing in their duties; he asked that distinguished ministers from the censorate and secretariat be appointed in their place.

sentences.zh: 仍遣使核其治行，其治最者則增秩，賜金幣。

translations.literal: He also dispatched envoys to verify their conduct in office; those whose governance was best received rank increases and gifts of gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent envoys to review their performance; those who governed best were promoted and rewarded with gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 遼、金、宋三史久未克修，至是太平力贊其事，為總裁官，修成之。

translations.literal: The histories of Liao, Jin, and Song had long gone unrevised; now Taiping strongly supported the undertaking, served as chief compiler, and brought the work to completion.
translations.idiomatic: The histories of Liao, Jin, and Song had long gone unfinished; Taiping now strongly backed the project, served as chief compiler, and brought it to completion.

sentences.zh: 時粟貴而金銀賤，太平請出官本，委官收市之，所得不貲，其後兵興，卒獲其用。

translations.literal: At that time grain was dear and gold and silver cheap; Taiping requested that the state advance capital and commission officials to buy them up on the market; the profit was immense, and when war broke out later it proved of great use.
translations.idiomatic: Grain was dear and gold and silver cheap; Taiping asked the state to advance capital and commission officials to buy bullion on the market. The profit was immense, and when war broke out later the hoard proved invaluable.

sentences.zh: 四年，升中書平章政事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Central Secretariat Vice Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to vice councilor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷宣徽院使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Xuanzhen Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made Xuanzhen Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 宣徽典飲膳，權勢橫索，太平取簿閱之，惟太常禮儀使阿剌不花一無所需，太平因言於帝，請擢居近職，且厚賜之。

translations.literal: The Xuanzhen Office managed food and drink, and the powerful extorted from it by force; Taiping took the ledgers and reviewed them — only Court of Imperial Sacrifices Commissioner Alabuhua had taken nothing; Taiping therefore spoke to the emperor, requesting his promotion to a post near the throne and generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanzhen Office managed the court's food and drink, and the powerful extorted from it at will. Taiping reviewed the ledgers and found that only Court of Imperial Sacrifices Commissioner Alabuhua had taken nothing; he spoke to the emperor, asking that Alabuhua be promoted to a post near the throne and richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 六年，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 故事，台端非國姓不以授，太平因辭，詔特賜姓而改其名。

translations.literal: By precedent the head of the censorate was not granted to anyone not of the imperial surname; Taiping therefore declined, and an edict specially granted him the surname and changed his name.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the head of the censorate went only to men of the imperial surname; Taiping declined, and an edict specially granted him the surname and changed his name.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷中書平章政事，班同列上。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Central Secretariat Vice Councilor, ranking above his colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to vice councilor of the Central Secretariat, ranking above his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 國王朵而只為左丞相，請於帝曰：「臣藉先臣之廕，蚤襲位國王，昧於國家之理，今備位宰相，非得太平不足與共事。」

translations.literal: Prince Duo'erzhi served as Left Councilor and petitioned the emperor, saying, "Your servant, relying on my forefather's grace, early inherited the rank of prince and was ignorant of statecraft; now holding the post of councillor, without Taiping I am not fit to share in governing."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Duo'erzhi, serving as Left Councilor, told the emperor, "I inherited my princely rank early through my father's grace and knew little of statecraft; now that I hold a councillor's post, I cannot govern without Taiping at my side."

sentences.zh: 十一月，拜太平左丞相，朵而只為右丞相。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Taiping was made Left Councilor and Duo'erzhi Right Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Taiping was made Left Councilor and Duo'erzhi Right Councilor.

sentences.zh: 太平辭，帝不允，仍詔示天下。

translations.literal: Taiping declined, but the emperor would not agree and still issued an edict proclaiming this to all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping declined, but the emperor would not hear of it and issued an edict proclaiming the appointment throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，詔修后妃、功臣傳，特命太平同監修國史，蓋異數也。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year an edict ordered the revision of the biographies of empresses and meritorious ministers, specially appointing Taiping to jointly supervise the revision of the national history — a signal honor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year an edict ordered the revision of the biographies of empresses and meritorious ministers and specially appointed Taiping to jointly supervise the national history — a rare honor.

sentences.zh: 太平請僧道有妻子者勒為民以減蠹耗，給校官俸以防虛冒，請賜經筵講官坐以崇聖學，立行都水監以治黃河。

translations.literal: Taiping requested that monks and Daoists who had wives be compelled to return to commoner status to reduce waste and corruption, that salaries be given to collation officers to prevent false claims, that seats be granted to lecturers at the Classics Collegium to honor sacred learning, and that a traveling Directorate-General of Waterways be established to manage the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping asked that monks and Daoists with wives be compelled to return to lay status to curb waste and fraud, that collation officers be paid salaries to prevent false claims, that lecturers at the Classics Collegium be granted seats to honor sacred learning, and that a traveling Directorate-General of Waterways be set up to manage the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 舉隱士完者篤、執禮哈郎、董立、張樞、李孝光。

translations.literal: He recommended the recluses Wanzhedu, Zhilihalang, Dong Li, Zhang Shu, and Li Xiaoguang.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended the recluses Wanzhedu, Zhilihalang, Dong Li, Zhang Shu, and Li Xiaoguang.

sentences.zh: 是時，天下無事，朝廷稽古禮文之典，有墜必舉。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was at peace; the court examined the ancient rites and ceremonial codes, and whatever had fallen into disuse was revived.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was at peace; the court turned to the ancient rites and ceremonial codes and revived whatever had fallen into disuse.

sentences.zh: 平生好訪問人才，不問南北，必記錄於冊，至是多進用之。

translations.literal: Throughout his life he delighted in seeking out men of talent, regardless of north or south, always recording them in his register; now many were advanced and employed.
translations.idiomatic: All his life he had sought out talent without regard to region, recording every name in his register; now many of those men were brought into office.

sentences.zh: 初，脫脫既罷相，出居西土。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Toqto'a had been dismissed from the councillorship, he went out to dwell in the western regions.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Toqto'a was dismissed from the councillorship, he withdrew to the western regions.

sentences.zh: 會其父馬札兒台卒，太平力請令脫脫歸葬，以全孝道。

translations.literal: When his father Majaritai died, Taiping strongly petitioned that Toqto'a be allowed to return for the funeral, to fulfill filial duty.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Majaritai died, Taiping strongly petitioned that Toqto'a be allowed home for the funeral and the full observance of filial duty.

sentences.zh: 左右以為難，太平曰：「脫脫乃心王室，大義滅親，今父歿而不克奔訃，為善者不幾於怠乎！」

translations.literal: Those around the emperor thought it difficult; Taiping said, "Toqto'a is loyal to the royal house and has set public duty above private kin; now that his father is dead and he cannot rush to the death announcement, would not those who do good nearly fall into neglect!"
translations.idiomatic: Those around the emperor objected that it would be difficult; Taiping said, "Toqto'a is loyal to the throne and has set public duty above private ties; if his father is dead and he cannot rush home, what man of virtue would not nearly fail in his duty!"

sentences.zh: 為之固請，以故脫脫得還。

translations.literal: He pressed the petition firmly, and for this reason Toqto'a was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the point firmly, and Toqto'a was allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 脫脫既得還朝，即拜為太傅，然不知太平之有德於己也，因汝中柏讒間成隙，遽欲中傷之。

translations.literal: Once Toqto'a had returned to court he was immediately made Grand Preceptor, yet he did not know that Taiping had shown him kindness; because of Ruizhong Bo's slander a rift arose, and he suddenly wished to strike at Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: Once Toqto'a returned to court he was immediately made Grand Preceptor, yet he did not know Taiping had done him a kindness; Ruizhong Bo's slander opened a rift between them, and Toqto'a suddenly sought to bring Taiping down.

sentences.zh: 是時，中書參政孔思立等皆一時名人，太平所拔用者，悉誣以罪黜去。

translations.literal: At that time among the Central Secretariat associate administrators Kong Sili and others were all men of renown of the age; those whom Taiping had advanced were all falsely charged with crimes and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Central Secretariat's associate administrators, Kong Sili and others were men of renown; every man Taiping had advanced was falsely charged and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 九年七月，罷為翰林學士承旨，既又誣劾其過失，而並論其子也先忽都不宜僭娶宗室女。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the ninth year he was dismissed to Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy; then they again falsely impeached him for faults, and also argued that his son Yexianhudou should not presumptuously marry a woman of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the ninth year he was demoted to Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy; then they falsely impeached him again and argued that his son Yexianhudou had no right to marry a woman of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 脫脫之母聞之，謂脫脫兄弟曰：「太平好人也，何害於汝而欲去之。

translations.literal: When Toqto'a's mother heard of this, she said to Toqto'a and his brothers, "Taiping is a good man — how does he harm you that you wish to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: When Toqto'a's mother heard of this, she told Toqto'a and his brothers, "Taiping is a good man — how has he harmed you that you wish to drive him out.

sentences.zh: 汝兄弟若違吾言，非吾子也。」

translations.literal: If you brothers disobey my words, you are not my sons."
translations.idiomatic: If you brothers disobey me, you are no sons of mine."

sentences.zh: 侍御史撒馬篤揚言於朝曰： 「御史欲害正人，壞台綱，如天下後世何？」

translations.literal: Palace censor Samadu declared openly at court, "The censors wish to harm upright men and destroy the integrity of the censorate — what of the realm and posterity?"
translations.idiomatic: Palace censor Samadu declared openly at court, "The censors wish to harm upright men and destroy the integrity of the censorate — what will become of the realm and posterity?"

sentences.zh: 即臥病不起。

translations.literal: He immediately took to his bed with illness and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately took to his bed and would not rise.

sentences.zh: 故吏田复勸太平自裁，太平曰：「吾無罪，當聽於天，若自殺，則誠有慊矣。」

translations.literal: His former clerk Tian Fu urged Taiping to take his own life; Taiping said, "I am without guilt and should await heaven's judgment; if I killed myself, I would truly have cause for regret."
translations.idiomatic: His former clerk Tian Fu urged Taiping to take his own life; Taiping said, "I am innocent and should await heaven's judgment; to kill myself would be a true cause for regret."

sentences.zh: 遂還奉元，杜門謝客，以書史自適。

translations.literal: He then returned to Fengyuan, shut his doors and refused visitors, and found contentment in books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Fengyuan, shut his doors to visitors, and found solace in books and histories.

sentences.zh: 河南盜起，十五年，詔命太平為江浙行省左丞相。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Henan, in the fifteenth year an edict appointed Taiping Left Councilor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Henan, an edict in the fifteenth year appointed Taiping Left Councilor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未行，改為淮南行省左丞相，兼知行樞密院事，總制諸軍，駐於濟寧。

translations.literal: Before he had set out, he was changed to Left Councilor of the Huainan Branch Secretariat, concurrently acting commissioner of the Privy Council, with overall command of all armies, stationed at Jining.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart he was reassigned as Left Councilor of the Huainan Branch Secretariat, concurrently acting commissioner of the Privy Council, with overall command of all armies, stationed at Jining.

sentences.zh: 時諸軍久出，糧餉苦不繼。

translations.literal: At that time the armies had been out long; grain supplies bitterly failed to continue.
translations.idiomatic: The armies had been in the field for a long time, and grain supplies could no longer keep pace.

sentences.zh: 太平命有司給牛具以種麥，自濟寧達於海州，民不擾而兵賴以濟。

translations.literal: Taiping ordered the officials to supply oxen and implements for planting wheat, from Jining reaching to Haizhou; the people were not disturbed and the troops relied on this for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping ordered officials to provide oxen and ploughs for wheat planting from Jining to Haizhou; the people were left undisturbed, and the armies were sustained.

sentences.zh: 議立土兵元帥府，輪番耕戰。

translations.literal: It was proposed to establish a native-troop marshal headquarters, rotating between farming and fighting.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed establishing marshal headquarters for local troops, who would rotate between farming and campaigning.

sentences.zh: 十六年，移鎮益都。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he moved his garrison to Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he transferred his command to Yidu.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除遼陽行省左丞相。

translations.literal: Before long, he was appointed Left Councillor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Left Councillor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 糴粟以給京師，處置有法，所致甚多而民不擾。

translations.literal: He purchased grain to supply the capital; his arrangements had method, what he procured was very great, yet the people were not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: He bought grain for the capital with disciplined methods, procured a great quantity, and still left the people undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 十七年五月，召為中書左丞相。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year, he was summoned to serve as Left Councillor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year he was recalled to serve as Left Councillor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時毛貴據山東，明年，由河間入寇，官軍屢敗，漸逼京都，中外大駭，廷議遷​​都以避之，和者如出一口。

translations.literal: At that time Mao Gui held Shandong; the next year he invaded through Hejian; government troops repeatedly suffered defeat and gradually pressed upon the capital; within and without the court were greatly alarmed; the court debated relocating the capital to avoid him, and those in agreement spoke as from one mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Gui then held Shandong; the next year he invaded through Hejian. Government troops suffered repeated defeats, and the rebels drew ever closer to the capital. Court and country were thrown into alarm, and the court debated moving the capital to escape him — nearly all spoke as one.

sentences.zh: 太平力爭以為不可，起同知樞密院事劉哈剌不花於彰德，引兵擊之，大敗賊眾，京城遂安。

translations.literal: Taiping forcefully argued that this could not be; he raised Liu Harbahua, Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council, at Zhangde, led troops to attack him, and utterly routed the rebel host; the capital was then secure.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping forcefully objected that this must not be done. He recalled Liu Harbahua, Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council, from Zhangde, led troops against the rebels, and routed them completely, and the capital was made safe.

sentences.zh: 會張士誠以浙西降，而晉、冀、關陝之間，察罕鐵木兒屢以捷奏聞。

translations.literal: Then Zhang Shicheng submitted with western Zhejiang, and between Shanxi, Hebei, and the Guanzhong region, Chaghan Temür repeatedly reported victories.
translations.idiomatic: About then Zhang Shicheng surrendered with western Zhejiang, while between Shanxi, Hebei, and the Guanzhong passes Chaghan Temür sent repeated reports of victory.

sentences.zh: 於是中外人心翕然，有中興之望矣。

translations.literal: Then the hearts of those within and without the court drew together as one, and there was hope for restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Hearts within and without the court drew together, and the realm looked toward restoration.

sentences.zh: 太平又考求，凡死節之臣，雖布衣亦加贈諡，有官者就官其子孫，人尤感動。

translations.literal: Taiping further investigated and sought out: for every minister who died in loyalty, even commoners were granted posthumous titles; those who held office had their descendants given their ranks — people were especially moved.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping further sought out every man who had died in loyalty: even commoners received posthumous titles, and where men had held office their descendants were given their ranks. People were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 當時右丞相搠思監家人以造偽鈔事覺，刑部欲連逮搠思監。

translations.literal: At that time the family of Right Councillor Choson was implicated in counterfeiting; the Ministry of Justice wished to implicate Choson as well.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the family of Right Councillor Choson was caught counterfeiting currency, and the Ministry of Justice sought to implicate Choson himself.

sentences.zh: 太平力為解之，曰：「堂堂宰相烏得有此事，四海聞之，若國體何！」

translations.literal: Taiping forcefully defended him, saying, "How could a grand councillor have such a thing — if the four seas hear of it, what of the dignity of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Taiping forcefully defended him, saying, "How could a grand councillor be guilty of such a thing — if the realm hears of it, what becomes of the dignity of the state."

sentences.zh: 搠思監既劾罷，太平所得俸祿多分饋之。

translations.literal: Choson having been impeached and dismissed, Taiping gave him much of his own salary.
translations.idiomatic: After Choson was impeached and dismissed, Taiping gave him much of his own salary.

sentences.zh: 二皇后奇氏與皇太子謀，欲內禪，遣宦者資正院使樸不花諭意於太平，太平不答。

translations.literal: Empress Qi and the Crown Prince plotted to abdicate the throne internally; they sent the eunuch Puhua, Commissioner of the Zizheng Court, to convey their intent to Taiping — Taiping did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qi and the Crown Prince plotted an internal abdication and sent the eunuch Puhua, Commissioner of the Zizheng Court, to convey their intent to Taiping. Taiping made no reply.

sentences.zh: 皇后又召太平至宮中，舉酒申前意，太平依違而已。

translations.literal: The empress again summoned Taiping to the palace, raised a cup and renewed her earlier intent; Taiping only hedged.
translations.idiomatic: The empress summoned Taiping again to the palace, raised a cup, and renewed her earlier proposal; Taiping only equivocated.

sentences.zh: 是時，皇太子欲盡逐帝近臣，又令監察御史劾帝親暱臣御史中丞禿魯鐵木兒, 未及奏而所劾御史被遷為他官，皇太子疑也先忽都洩其事，益決意去太平政柄。

translations.literal: At that time the Crown Prince wished to drive out all the emperor's close ministers; he also had investigating censors impeach the emperor's intimate, Censor-in-Chief Tolu Temür; before the memorial could be submitted the impeaching censor was transferred to another post; the Crown Prince suspected Yexianhudu had leaked the matter and was all the more resolved to remove Taiping from power.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince then sought to drive out all the emperor's close ministers and had investigating censors impeach the emperor's intimate, Censor-in-Chief Tolu Temür. Before the memorial could be submitted, the impeaching censor was transferred elsewhere. The Crown Prince suspected Yexianhudu had leaked the affair and grew all the more determined to strip Taiping of power.

sentences.zh: 知樞密院事紐的該聞而歎曰：「善人國之紀也，苟去之，國將何賴乎！」

translations.literal: Niudigai, Commissioner of the Privy Council, heard and sighed, saying, "Good men are the cords of the state; if they are removed, upon what can the state rely."
translations.idiomatic: Niudigai, Commissioner of the Privy Council, heard of this and sighed, "Good men are the cords of the state; if they are cast aside, upon what can the state rely."

sentences.zh: 數於帝前左右之，以故皇太子之志未及逞。

translations.literal: Several times before the emperor he spoke on Taiping's behalf, and for this reason the Crown Prince's design had not yet been carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Several times he spoke for Taiping before the emperor, and so the Crown Prince's design had not yet been carried out.

sentences.zh: 會紐的該死，皇太子遂令監察御史買住、桑哥失理劾左丞成遵、參政趙中等下獄死，以二人為太平黨也。

translations.literal: Then Niudigai died; the Crown Prince then had investigating censors Maizhu and Sangge Shili impeach Left Administrator Cheng Zun and Associate Administrator Zhao Zhong and others, who were imprisoned and put to death, on the ground that the two were of Taiping's faction.
translations.idiomatic: When Niudigai died, the Crown Prince had investigating censors Maizhu and Sangge Shili impeach Left Administrator Cheng Zun and Associate Administrator Zhao Zhong and others; they were thrown into prison and put to death as men of Taiping's faction.

sentences.zh: 太平知勢有不可留，數以疾辭位。

translations.literal: Taiping knew the situation could not be stayed; several times he pleaded illness and resigned his post.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping saw that he could not remain; several times he pleaded illness and asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 二十年二月，拜太保，俾養疾於家。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twentieth year, he was appointed Grand Preceptor and ordered to nurse his illness at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twentieth year he was made Grand Preceptor and ordered to recover his health at home.

sentences.zh: 台臣奏言以謂當​​時事之艱危，政賴賢材之宏濟，太平以師保兼相職為宜。

translations.literal: Censorate officials memorialized, saying that given the peril of the times, governance relied on great talent for broad relief; Taiping should hold the post of tutor and guardian while also serving as councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Censorate officials memorialized that in the peril of the times governance depended on great talent, and that Taiping should serve as tutor and guardian while also holding a councillor's post.

sentences.zh: 帝不能從。

translations.literal: The emperor could not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not agree.

sentences.zh: 會陽翟王阿魯輝鐵木兒倡亂，騷動北邊，勢逼上都，皇太子乃言於帝，命太平留守上都，實欲置之死地。

translations.literal: Then Prince Aluhui Temür of Yangzhai raised rebellion, disturbing the northern frontier and pressing upon Shangdu; the Crown Prince spoke to the emperor and ordered Taiping to remain and guard Shangdu — in truth intending to place him in mortal peril.
translations.idiomatic: Then Prince Aluhui Temür of Yangzhai raised rebellion, roiling the northern frontier and threatening Shangdu. The Crown Prince spoke to the emperor and ordered Taiping to remain and guard Shangdu — in truth intending to send him to his death.

sentences.zh: 太平遂往。

translations.literal: Taiping then went.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping went.

sentences.zh: 有同知太常院事脫歡者，也先忽都故將也，聞陽翟王將至，乃引兵縛王至軍前，太平不受，令生致闕下，北邊以寧。

translations.literal: There was one Toghan, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, a former general of Yexianhudu; hearing that the Prince of Yangzhai was about to arrive, he led troops and bound the prince before the army; Taiping would not accept this and ordered him delivered alive to the court; the northern frontier was then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Toghan, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and a former general of Yexianhudu, heard that the Prince of Yangzhai was approaching, led troops, and bound the prince before the army. Taiping would not accept this and ordered the prince delivered alive to court, and the northern frontier was pacified.

sentences.zh: 太平終不以為己功。

translations.literal: Taiping to the end did not regard this as his own achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping never claimed the credit for himself.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔拜太傅，賜田若干頃，俾歸奉元。

translations.literal: Before long, an edict appointed him Grand Tutor, granted him several qing of fields, and ordered him to return to Fengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict appointed him Grand Tutor, granted him several qing of land, and ordered him to return to Fengyuan.

sentences.zh: 帝欲以伯撒里為丞相，伯撒里辭曰：「臣老不足以任宰相，陛下必以命臣，非得太平同事不可。」

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make Bersar councillor; Bersar declined, saying, "Your servant is too old to bear the burden of councillor; if Your Majesty must command me, I cannot do so unless Taiping serves with me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to make Bersar councillor. Bersar declined, saying, "I am too old to bear the burden of councillor; if Your Majesty must command me, I cannot serve unless Taiping serves at my side."

sentences.zh: 於是密旨令伯撒里留太平毋行。

translations.literal: Then a secret edict ordered Bersar to keep Taiping from departing.
translations.idiomatic: A secret edict then ordered Bersar to keep Taiping from leaving.

sentences.zh: 太平至沙井，聞命而止，宿留久之。

translations.literal: Taiping reached Shajing, heard the order, and stopped; he lingered there for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping reached Shajing, heard the order, and halted; he lingered there a long while.

sentences.zh: 皇太子惡其既去而復留也，二十三年，令御史大夫普化劾太平故違上命，當正其罪。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince hated that he had left yet returned to stay; in the twenty-third year he had Censor-in-Chief Puhua impeach Taiping for deliberately disobeying the imperial command, saying his crime should be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince resented that Taiping had left and then returned to stay. In the twenty-third year he had Censor-in-Chief Puhua impeach Taiping for deliberately defying the imperial command and demand that his crime be punished.

sentences.zh: 詔乃悉拘所授宣命及所賜物，俾往陝西之西居焉。

translations.literal: An edict then confiscated all appointment patents and gifts granted him and ordered him to dwell in the far west of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict confiscated every patent of appointment and every gift he had received and ordered him to dwell in the far west of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 搠思監因誣奏之，安置土蕃，尋遣使者逼令自裁。

translations.literal: Choson then falsely memorialized against him; he was resettled in Tibet, and soon an envoy was sent to compel him to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: Choson then falsely memorialized against him; he was resettled in Tibet, and soon an envoy was sent to compel him to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 太平至東勝，賦詩一篇，乃自殺。

translations.literal: Taiping reached Dongsheng, composed one poem, and then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiping reached Dongsheng he composed a poem and then took his own life.

sentences.zh: 年六十三。

translations.literal: He was sixty-three years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，監察御史辯其非辜，請加褒贈。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, an investigating censor argued that he had been innocent and requested posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year an investigating censor argued that he had been innocent and petitioned for posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 也先忽都，名均，字公秉。

translations.literal: Yexianhudu, personal name Jun, courtesy name Gongbing.
translations.idiomatic: Yexianhudu, personal name Jun, courtesy name Gongbing.

sentences.zh: 少好學，有俊才，累遷殿中侍御史、治書侍御史、翰林侍讀學士，皆兼襲虎賁親軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and had outstanding talent; he was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant Censor, Investigating Censor, and Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Waiting, each time also inheriting the post of Commander-in-Chief of the Huben Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and had outstanding talent. He rose through the posts of Palace Attendant Censor, Investigating Censor, and Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Waiting, each time also inheriting the command of the Huben Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 太平之為相也，務廣延才彥，而也先忽都以丞相子，又傾己下士，以故名稱籍然。

translations.literal: When Taiping served as councillor he strove to extend employment to men of talent; Yexianhudu, as the councillor's son, also humbled himself before scholars, and for this his reputation was widely known.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiping served as councillor he strove to gather men of talent; Yexianhudu, as the councillor's son, likewise humbled himself before scholars, and his name became widely known.

sentences.zh: 已而被劾罷，從親還奉元。

translations.literal: Later he was impeached and dismissed, and returned to Fengyuan with his kin.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was impeached and dismissed and returned to Fengyuan with his family.

sentences.zh: 居六年，召為兵部尚書、同知樞密院事，除通政院使。

translations.literal: After six years he was summoned to serve as Minister of War and Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council, then appointed Commissioner of the Tongzheng Court.
translations.idiomatic: After six years he was recalled as Minister of War and Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council, then appointed Commissioner of the Tongzheng Court.

sentences.zh: 太平再相，授知樞密院事，遷太子詹事。

translations.literal: When Taiping again became councillor, he was appointed Commissioner of the Privy Council and promoted to Supervisor of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiping again became councillor, he was appointed Commissioner of the Privy Council and promoted to Supervisor of the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 十九年，群盜由開平東屯遼陽。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, bandits from the east of Kaiping encamped at Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year bandits encamped at Liaoyang after advancing from east of Kaiping.

sentences.zh: 冬，詔也先忽都以知樞密院事兼太子詹事率師往討。

translations.literal: In winter, an edict ordered Yexianhudu, as Commissioner of the Privy Council and Supervisor of the Crown Prince's Household, to lead troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: That winter an edict ordered Yexianhudu, as Commissioner of the Privy Council and Supervisor of the Crown Prince's Household, to lead troops against them.

sentences.zh: 太平以其年少，數請改命，不允。

translations.literal: Taiping, because he was still young, repeatedly petitioned to change the appointment; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping, thinking him too young, repeatedly petitioned to have the appointment changed, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 至則遣將拔懿州省治，盜逾遼河東奔。

translations.literal: When he arrived he sent generals to capture Yizhou provincial seat; the bandits crossed the Liao River and fled east.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he sent generals to capture the Yizhou provincial seat; the bandits crossed the Liao River and fled east.

sentences.zh: 而朝廷讒構日甚，罷為上都留守。

translations.literal: But slander in court grew daily worse, and he was dismissed to serve as Keeper of Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: But slander at court grew daily worse, and he was demoted to Keeper of Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 尋改宣政院使，以丁內艱不起。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Commissioner of the Xuanzheng Court, but because of mourning for his mother he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Commissioner of the Xuanzheng Court, but mourning for his mother kept him from taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 搠思監再相，復奏強起之，即日監察御史也帖木、李好直又劾罷之。

translations.literal: When Choson again became councillor, he again memorialized to force his recall; that very day investigating censors Yetiemur and Li Haozhi again impeached him and had him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Choson again became councillor, he memorialized to force Yexianhudu's recall; that same day investigating censors Yetiemur and Li Haozhi impeached him again and had him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 已而搠思監徇皇太子旨，構成大獄，誣老的沙、蠻子、按難達識理、沙加識理​​、也先忽都及脫歡等不軌，執脫歡煅煉其獄，連逮不已。

translations.literal: Before long Choson, following the Crown Prince's intent, fabricated a great case, falsely charging Laodesha, Manzi, Anundashili, Shajiashili, Yexianhudu, Toghan, and others with sedition; they seized Toghan and tortured him to extract confession, and the chain of arrests did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Choson, at the Crown Prince's bidding, fabricated a great case, falsely charging Laodesha, Manzi, Anundashili, Shajiashili, Yexianhudu, Toghan, and others with sedition. They seized Toghan and tortured him for confession, and the chain of arrests went on without end.

sentences.zh: 帝知其無辜，欲釋其事，特命大赦。

translations.literal: The emperor knew they were innocent and wished to release the matter; he specially ordered a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew they were innocent and wished to quash the affair; he specially ordered a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 而搠思監增入條畫內，獨不赦前獄。

translations.literal: But Choson added a provision within the terms, alone not pardoning the earlier case.
translations.idiomatic: Choson added a provision to the terms that alone excluded the earlier case from pardon.

sentences.zh: 唯老的沙逃於孛羅鐵木兒大同軍中，蠻子、按難達識理等遂皆貶死。

translations.literal: Only Laodesha escaped to the army of Boluo Temür at Datong; Manzi, Anundashili, and the others were all banished and put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Only Laodesha escaped to Boluo Temür's army at Datong; Manzi, Anundashili, and the others were banished and put to death.

sentences.zh: 也先忽都當貶撒思嘉之地，道由朵思麻，行宣政院使桓州閭素受知太平，因留居其地。

translations.literal: Yexianhudu was to be banished to the land of Sasiq; passing through Duosima, Huanzhou Lu, Commissioner of the Xuanzheng Court, who had long been known to Taiping, therefore kept him to dwell in that place.
translations.idiomatic: Yexianhudu was to be banished to Sasiq; passing through Duosima, Huanzhou Lu, Commissioner of the Xuanzheng Court, who had long been favored by Taiping, kept him to dwell there.

sentences.zh: 執政知其故，奏也先忽都違命，杖死之。

translations.literal: The chief ministers, knowing the reason, memorialized that Yexianhudu had disobeyed the command and had him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers, knowing the reason, memorialized that Yexianhudu had disobeyed his orders and had him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 年四十四。

translations.literal: He was forty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-four.

sentences.zh: 有詩集十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected poetry in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected poetry in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 鐵木兒塔識

translations.literal: Tiemuertashi
translations.idiomatic: Tiemuertashi

sentences.zh: 鐵木兒塔識，字九齡，國王脫脫之子。

translations.literal: Tiemuertashi, courtesy name Jiuling, was the son of King Toqto'a.
translations.idiomatic: Tiemuertashi, styled Jiuling, was the son of King Toqto'a.

sentences.zh: 資禀宏偉，補國子學諸生，讀書穎悟絕人。

translations.literal: His native endowment was grand and imposing; he entered the Imperial Academy as a student and in reading was exceptionally quick beyond others.
translations.idiomatic: Grand and imposing by nature, he entered the Imperial Academy and in his reading proved exceptionally quick beyond other men.

sentences.zh: 事明宗於潛邸。

translations.literal: He served Emperor Mingzong at the Hidden Residence.
translations.idiomatic: He served Emperor Mingzong at the Hidden Residence.

sentences.zh: 文宗初，由同知都護府事累遷禮部尚書，進參議中書省事，擢陝西行台侍御史，留為奎章閣侍書學士，除大都留守，尋同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wenzong's reign, from Vice Director of the Capital Protection Office he was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Rites, advanced to Associate Administrator of the Central Secretariat, promoted to Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, retained as Academician Scribe of the Kuizhang Pavilion, appointed Keeper of Dadu, and soon Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Wenzong's reign he rose from Vice Director of the Capital Protection Office through Minister of Rites to Associate Administrator of the Central Secretariat, then to Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat; he was retained as Academician Scribe of the Kuizhang Pavilion, appointed Keeper of Dadu, and soon made Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 後至元六年，拜中書右丞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Zhiyuan era of Emperor Shundi, he was appointed Right Vice Councillor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Zhiyuan era he was appointed Right Vice Councillor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至正改元，昇平章政事。

translations.literal: When the Zhizheng era began, he was promoted to Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhizheng era began he was promoted to Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 伯顏罷相，庶務多所更張，鐵木兒塔識盡心輔贊。

translations.literal: When Bayan was dismissed from the councillorship, many affairs were greatly changed; Tiemuertashi devoted himself to assisting and supporting him.
translations.idiomatic: When Bayan was dismissed from the councillorship and many policies were overturned, Tiemuertashi devoted himself to assisting the new order.

sentences.zh: 每入番直，帝為出宿宣文閣，賜坐榻前，詢以政道，必夜分乃罷。

translations.literal: Whenever he entered palace duty, the emperor would leave the Xuanwen Pavilion to receive him, grant him a seat before the couch, and inquire about governance; only at midnight would they break off.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he came on palace duty the emperor would leave the Xuanwen Pavilion to receive him, grant him a seat before the couch, and inquire about governance until midnight.

sentences.zh: 二年，郊，鐵木兒塔識言大祀竣事，必有實惠及民，以當天心，乃賜民明年田租之半。

translations.literal: In the second year, at the suburban sacrifice, Tiemuertashi said that when the great rite was completed there must be real benefit reaching the people to accord with Heaven's heart; he therefore granted the people half of next year's land tax.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, after the suburban sacrifice, Tiemuertashi argued that a great rite must bring real benefit to the people if it was to accord with Heaven's heart; half of the next year's land tax was therefore remitted.

sentences.zh: 嶺北地寒，不任穡事，歲募富民和糴為邊餉，民雖稍利，而費官鹽為多。

translations.literal: The northern frontier lands were cold and could not bear grain work; each year wealthy households were recruited for coordinated grain purchase as frontier supplies; though the people gained somewhat, official salt was expended in great measure.
translations.idiomatic: The northern frontier was too cold for grain farming; each year wealthy households were recruited for coordinated grain purchases to supply the border. The people gained somewhat, but at great cost in official salt.

sentences.zh: 鐵木兒塔識乃請別輸京倉米百萬斛，儲於和林以為備。

translations.literal: Tiemuertashi then requested that a separate million hu of grain from the capital granaries be transported and stored at Karakorum as reserve.
translations.idiomatic: Tiemuertashi then petitioned that a separate million hu of grain from the capital granaries be stored at Karakorum as a reserve.

sentences.zh: 日本商百餘人遇風漂入高麗，高麗掠其貨，表請沒入其人以為奴。

translations.literal: More than a hundred Japanese merchants, meeting wind, were driven into Goryeo; Goryeo seized their goods and memorialized requesting that the people be confiscated and made slaves.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred Japanese merchants were driven by wind into Goryeo; Goryeo seized their goods and memorialized asking that the men be confiscated and made slaves.

sentences.zh: 鐵木兒塔識持不可，曰：「天子一視同仁，豈宜乘人之險以為利？

translations.literal: Tiemuertashi held that this could not be, saying, "The Son of Heaven treats all alike with equal kindness — how can one take advantage of another's peril for profit?
translations.idiomatic: Tiemuertashi objected, saying, "The Son of Heaven treats all alike with equal kindness — how can one take advantage of another's peril for profit?

sentences.zh: 宜資其還。」

translations.literal: They should be supplied for their return."
translations.idiomatic: They should be supplied for their return."

sentences.zh: 已而日本果上表稱謝。

translations.literal: Before long Japan indeed sent up a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Japan did send up a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 俄有日本僧告其國遣人刺探國事者。

translations.literal: Soon a Japanese monk reported that his country had sent men to spy on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a Japanese monk reported that his country had sent men to spy on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 鐵木兒塔識曰：「刺探在敵國固有之，今六合一家，何以刺探為？

translations.literal: Tiemuertashi said, "Spying exists even among enemy states; now the six directions are one household — why speak of spying?
translations.idiomatic: Tiemuertashi said, "Spying exists even among enemy states; now all under Heaven is one household — why speak of spying?

sentences.zh: 設果有之，正可令睹中國之盛，歸告其主，使知向化。」

translations.literal: If there truly were such men, they could simply be allowed to witness China's greatness and return to report to their lord, so that he might know to turn toward civilization."
translations.idiomatic: If such men truly existed, they should be allowed to witness China's greatness and return to tell their lord, so that he might know to turn toward civilization."

sentences.zh: 兩浙、閩鹽額累增而課愈虧，江浙行省請減額，鐵木兒塔識奏歲減十三萬引。

translations.literal: The salt quota in the Two Zhe and Fujian was repeatedly increased yet revenue grew ever more deficient; the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat requested reduction of the quota, and Tiemuertashi memorialized a yearly reduction of one hundred thirty thousand yin.
translations.idiomatic: The salt quota in the Two Zhe and Fujian was repeatedly raised yet revenue fell ever further short; the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat requested a reduction, and Tiemuertashi memorialized an annual cut of one hundred thirty thousand yin.

sentences.zh: 五年，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 務以靜重持大體，不為苛嬈以立聲威。

translations.literal: He strove to maintain calm weight and uphold the larger pattern, and did not rely on harsh vexation to establish reputation and authority.
translations.idiomatic: He strove to uphold the larger pattern with calm weight and did not rely on harsh measures to build a reputation for authority.

sentences.zh: 建言：「近歲大臣獲罪，重者族滅，輕者籍其妻孥。

translations.literal: He offered a memorial, saying, "In recent years great ministers who were condemned — in heavy cases their clans were exterminated, in light cases their wives and children were registered;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, saying, "In recent years condemned great ministers — in the gravest cases their clans were exterminated, in lighter cases their wives and children were registered;

sentences.zh: 祖宗聖訓，父子罪不相及。

translations.literal: The sage instruction of the ancestors held that the crimes of fathers and sons did not extend to one another.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral teaching held that the crimes of fathers and sons did not extend to one another.

sentences.zh: 請除之。」

translations.literal: I request that this be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Let this be abolished.

sentences.zh: 著為令。

translations.literal: It was established as a statute.
translations.idiomatic: The request was enacted as law.

sentences.zh: 近畿饑民爭赴京城，奏出贓罰鈔，糴米萬石，即近郊寺觀為糜食之，所活不可勝計。

translations.literal: Hungry people near the capital rushed to the city; he memorialized to release confiscated and penal currency, purchase ten thousand shi of rice, and immediately at suburban temples and monasteries prepare gruel for them; those who were saved could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Hungry people near the capital rushed into the city; he memorialized to release confiscated and penal funds, buy ten thousand shi of rice, and set up gruel kitchens at suburban temples and monasteries; the number of lives saved could not be counted.

sentences.zh: 居歲餘，遷平章政事，位居第一。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Grand Councillor, ranking first.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year he was transferred to Grand Councillor, ranking first.

sentences.zh: 大駕時巡，留鎮大都。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage toured at times, he remained to guard Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured, he remained to guard Dadu.

sentences.zh: 舊法：細民糴於官倉，出印券，月給之者，其直三百文，謂之紅貼米；

translations.literal: The old law: common people who purchased from government granaries received stamped certificates and were given grain monthly at three hundred wen per unit — this was called red-coupon rice;
translations.idiomatic: Under the old law, common people who bought from government granaries received stamped certificates and were given grain monthly at three hundred wen per unit — this was called red-coupon rice;

sentences.zh: 賦籌而給之，盡三月止者，其直五百文，謂之散籌米。

translations.literal: those who paid tally-chits and were given grain for three months only paid five hundred wen per unit — this was called scattered-tally rice.
translations.idiomatic: those who paid tally-chits and received grain for only three months paid five hundred wen per unit — this was called scattered-tally rice.

sentences.zh: 貪民買其籌貼以為利。

translations.literal: Greedy people bought their tallies and coupons for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy men bought up the tallies and coupons for profit.

sentences.zh: 鐵木兒塔識請別發米二十萬石，遣官坐市肆，使人持五十文即得米一升，姦弊遂絕。

translations.literal: Tiemuertashi requested that a separate two hundred thousand shi of grain be issued, officials stationed in market shops, and people holding fifty wen could obtain one sheng of rice; the abuses were then ended.
translations.idiomatic: Tiemuertashi petitioned that a separate two hundred thousand shi of grain be issued, officials posted in market shops, and anyone holding fifty wen receive one sheng of rice; the abuses were then ended.

sentences.zh: 七年，首相去位，帝召鐵木兒塔識諭旨，若曰：「爾先人事我先朝，顯有勞績，爾實能世其家，今命汝為左丞相。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when the chief councillor left his post, the emperor summoned Tiemuertashi and conveyed the intent, as if to say, "Your forebear served my former dynasty with manifest merit; you truly can carry on your house; now I appoint you Left Councillor."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when the chief councillor left office, the emperor summoned Tiemuertashi and said, "Your forebear served my former dynasty with manifest merit; you truly can carry on your house. I now appoint you Left Councillor."

sentences.zh: 鐵木兒塔識叩頭固辭，不允，乃拜命。

translations.literal: Tiemuertashi kowtowed and firmly declined; it was not granted, and he then accepted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Tiemuertashi kowtowed and firmly declined, but the emperor would not hear of it, and he accepted the appointment.

sentences.zh: 鐵木兒塔識修飭綱紀，立內外通調之法：朝官外補，許得陛辭，親授帝訓，責以成效；

translations.literal: Tiemuertashi repaired and ordered the statutes, establishing a law of mutual transfer between inner and outer service: for court officials appointed to outer posts, audience for leave-taking was permitted, the emperor's instruction was personally conferred, and they were charged with results;
translations.idiomatic: Tiemuertashi restored discipline and established a law of mutual transfer between court and provinces: court officials sent to outer posts were granted audience for leave-taking, received the emperor's instruction in person, and were charged with results;

sentences.zh: 郡邑賢能吏，次第甄拔，入補朝闕。

translations.literal: worthy and able officials of commanderies and districts were selected in order and entered to fill vacancies at court.
translations.idiomatic: worthy and able officials of the commanderies and districts were selected in turn to fill vacancies at court.

sentences.zh: 分海漕米四十萬石置沿河諸倉，以備凶荒。

translations.literal: He divided four hundred thousand shi of sea-transport grain and placed it in granaries along the river as reserve against famine.
translations.idiomatic: He set aside four hundred thousand shi of sea-transport grain in granaries along the river as a reserve against famine.

sentences.zh: 先是，僧人與齊民均受役於官，其法中變，至是奏復其舊。

translations.literal: Earlier, Buddhist monks and common people alike had borne corvée service to the government; the law had changed in the middle; now he memorialized to restore the old practice.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Buddhist monks and common people alike had borne corvée to the government; the law had been altered in the meantime, and now he memorialized to restore the old practice.

sentences.zh: 孔子後襲封衍聖公，階止四品，奏升為三品。

translations.literal: Confucius's descendant who inherited the title Duke Yansheng had a rank stopping at the fourth grade; he memorialized to raise it to the third grade.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke Yansheng, Confucius's hereditary heir, held rank only at the fourth grade; he memorialized to raise it to the third.

sentences.zh: 歲一再詣國學，進諸生而獎勵之。

translations.literal: Each year he went once or twice to the Imperial Academy, advanced the students, and rewarded and encouraged them.
translations.idiomatic: Each year he visited the Imperial Academy once or twice to honor the students and encourage them.

sentences.zh: 中書故事，用老臣預議大政，久廢不設，鐵木兒塔識奏復其規，起腆合、張元樸等四人為議事平章。

translations.literal: Central Secretariat precedent called for aged ministers to participate in deliberating major affairs; long abolished and not established, Tiemuertashi memorialized to restore the regulation and raised Tienhe, Zhang Yuanpu, and four others as deliberative grand councillors.
translations.idiomatic: By Central Secretariat precedent, aged ministers had once taken part in deliberating major affairs; the practice had long been abandoned. Tiemuertashi memorialized to restore it and appointed Tienhe, Zhang Yuanpu, and four others as deliberative grand councillors.

sentences.zh: 曾未半年，救偏補弊之政以次興舉，中外咸悅。

translations.literal: Before half a year had passed, policies to remedy partiality and repair deficiencies were raised in succession; within and without were all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: In less than half a year, remedial reforms were launched one after another, and court and country alike rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 從幸上京還，入政事堂甫一日，俄感暴疾薨。

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor on the journey to the Upper Capital and returning, he entered the Hall of Government Affairs for only one day when suddenly stricken with a violent illness he died.
translations.idiomatic: After accompanying the emperor to the Upper Capital and back, he entered the Hall of Government Affairs for only a day before he was suddenly stricken with a violent illness and died.

sentences.zh: 年四十六。

translations.literal: Age forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈開誠濟美同德翊運功臣、太師、中書右丞相，追封冀寧王，諡文忠。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted the title of meritorious minister Kaicheng Jimei Tongde Yiyun, Grand Preceptor, and Right Councillor of the Central Secretariat; posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Jining; posthumous title Wenzho.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title of meritorious minister Kaicheng Jimei Tongde Yiyun, Grand Preceptor, and Right Councillor of the Central Secretariat, enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Jining, with the posthumous title Wenzho.

sentences.zh: 鐵木兒塔識天性忠亮，學術正大，伊、洛諸儒之書，深所研究。

translations.literal: Tiemuertashi was by nature loyal and upright; his learning was orthodox and great; the books of the Yi-Luo scholars he deeply investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Tiemuertashi was loyal and upright by nature, his scholarship broad and upright, and he studied deeply the works of the Yi-Luo school.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問為治何先，對曰：「法祖宗。」

translations.literal: The emperor once asked what should come first in governing; he replied: "Emulate the ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked what should come first in governing. He replied, "Emulate the ancestors."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「王文統奇才也，朕恨不得如斯人者用之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Wang Wensun is a rare talent; I regret that I cannot find someone like him to employ."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Wang Wensun is a rare talent. I only wish I could find someone like him to employ."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「世祖有堯、舜之資，文統不以王道告君，而乃尚霸術，要近利，世祖之罪人也。

translations.literal: He replied: "Emperor Shizu had the capacity of Yao and Shun; Wensun did not counsel his lord with the kingly Way but instead prized hegemonic arts and sought near-term profit — he was a criminal against Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Emperor Shizu had the makings of Yao and Shun. Wensun did not counsel his lord with the kingly Way but instead prized hegemonic arts and sought immediate profit — he was Shizu's betrayer.

sentences.zh: 使今有文統，正當遠之，又何足取乎！」

translations.literal: If there were a Wensun today, he ought rightly to be kept at a distance — what would there be to esteem in him!"
translations.idiomatic: If there were a Wensun today, he ought rightly to be kept at a distance. What would there be to esteem in him!"

sentences.zh: 初，伯顏議罷科舉，鐵木兒塔識時在參議府，訖不署奏牘，及入中書，乃議復行之。

translations.literal: Initially, when Bayan proposed abolishing the civil examinations, Tiemuertashi was then in the Deliberation Office and never signed the memorial; when he entered the Central Secretariat, he then proposed restoring them.
translations.idiomatic: When Bayan proposed abolishing the civil examinations, Tiemuertashi was then in the Deliberation Office and refused to sign the memorial. Once he entered the Central Secretariat, he proposed restoring the examinations.

sentences.zh: 徵用處士，待以不次之擢。

translations.literal: He summoned and employed recluses, treating them with exceptional promotions.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned recluses to office and promoted them out of turn.

sentences.zh: 或疑為太優，鐵木兒塔識曰：「隱士無求於朝廷，朝廷有求於隱士，區區名爵，奚足惜哉！」

translations.literal: Some doubted this was too generous; Tiemuertashi said: "Recluses have no request of the court; the court has a request of recluses — what are petty titles and ranks that they should be grudged!"
translations.idiomatic: Some thought this too generous. Tiemuertashi said, "Recluses ask nothing of the court; the court asks something of recluses. Why begrudge them petty titles and ranks!"

sentences.zh: 識者誦之。

translations.literal: Those of discernment repeated his words.
translations.idiomatic: Men of discernment repeated his words.

sentences.zh: 時修遼、金、宋三史，鐵木兒塔識為總裁官，多所協贊云。

translations.literal: When the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song were being compiled, Tiemuertashi served as chief director and contributed much to their completion.
