translations.idiomatic: While the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song were being compiled, Tiemuertashi served as chief director and contributed much to the work.

sentences.zh: 達識帖睦邇

translations.literal: Dashitiemuer
translations.idiomatic: Dashitiemuer

sentences.zh: 達識帖睦邇，字九成。

translations.literal: Dashitiemuer, courtesy name Jiucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dashitiemuer, styled Jiucheng.

sentences.zh: 幼與其兄鐵木兒塔識俱入國學為諸生，讀經史，悉能通大義，尤好學書。

translations.literal: In youth he and his elder brother Tiemuertashi both entered the Imperial Academy as students; reading the Classics and histories, they could all comprehend the great principles, and he was especially fond of studying books.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he and his elder brother Tiemuertashi both entered the Imperial Academy as students. They read the Classics and histories and grasped their larger meaning; he was especially devoted to learning.

sentences.zh: 初以世冑補官，為太府監提點，擢治書侍御史，以言罷。

translations.literal: Initially by hereditary privilege he received an appointment, becoming intendant of the Imperial Household Commission; he was promoted to investigating censor but was dismissed on account of his memorializing.
translations.idiomatic: At first he received office through hereditary privilege as intendant of the Imperial Household Commission. He was promoted to investigating censor, then dismissed because of his memorials.

sentences.zh: 除樞密院同知，升中書右丞、翰林承旨，遷大司農。

translations.literal: Appointed associate administrator of the Privy Council; promoted to Central Secretariat vice councilor and Hanlin Academy chancellor; transferred to Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed associate administrator of the Privy Council, promoted to Central Secretariat vice councilor and Hanlin Academy chancellor, and then transferred to Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 至正七年，出為江浙行省平章政事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhizheng, he went out as Grand Councillor of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhizheng he was posted as Grand Councillor of the Jiangzhe branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，又入為大司農。

translations.literal: The next year he re-entered service as Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he returned to the capital as Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 九年，為湖廣行省平章政事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he became Grand Councillor of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he became Grand Councillor of the Huguang branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 沅、靖、柳、桂等路徭、獠竊發，朝廷以溪洞險阻，下詔招諭之。

translations.literal: Rebellions broke out among the Yao and Liao in Yuan, Jing, Liu, Gui, and other circuits; the court, because the stream-cave regions were perilous and obstructive, issued an edict summoning and persuading them to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao and Liao rose in revolt in Yuan, Jing, Liu, Gui, and other circuits. Because the stream-cave country was rugged and hard to reach, the court issued an edict summoning them to submit.

sentences.zh: 達識帖睦邇謂：「寇情不可料，請置三分省，一治靜江，一治沅、靖，一治柳、桂，以左右丞、參政分兵鎮其地。

translations.literal: Dashitiemuer said: "The bandits' situation cannot be predicted; I request establishing three branch secretariats — one administering Jingjiang, one administering Yuan and Jing, one administering Liu and Gui — with left and right vice directors and associate councillors dividing troops to guard those territories.
translations.idiomatic: Dashitiemuer said, "The rebels' movements cannot be foreseen. I request three branch secretariats — one at Jingjiang, one at Yuan and Jing, one at Liu and Gui — with left and right vice directors and associate councillors each commanding troops to hold the region.

sentences.zh: 罷靖州路總管府，改立靖州軍民安撫司，設萬戶府，益以戍兵。」

translations.literal: Abolish the Jingzhou Circuit pacification commission, establish in its stead the Jingzhou Military-Civilian Pacification Commission, set up a wanhu office, and augment with garrison troops."
translations.idiomatic: Abolish the Jingzhou circuit pacification commission and establish in its place the Jingzhou Military-Civilian Pacification Commission, set up a wanhu office, and add garrison troops."

sentences.zh: 朝廷皆如其言。

translations.literal: The court did all as he said.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved all of this.

sentences.zh: 已而諸徭、獠悉降，召還，復為大司農。

translations.literal: Before long all the Yao and Liao submitted; he was recalled and again became Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long all the Yao and Liao submitted. He was recalled and again made Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 十一年，台州方國珍起海上。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Fang Guozhen rose on the sea at Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Fang Guozhen rose on the sea off Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 達識帖睦邇奉詔與江浙行省參知政事樊執敬往招諭之。

translations.literal: Dashitiemuer received the edict and together with Fan Zhijing, associate chief minister of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat, went to summon and persuade him to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Dashitiemuer received an edict and, together with Fan Zhijing, associate chief minister of the Jiangzhe branch secretariat, went to summon and persuade him to submit.

sentences.zh: 明年，盜起河南。

translations.literal: The next year, bandits rose in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The next year bandits rose in Henan.

sentences.zh: 拜河南行省平章政事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Councillor of the Henan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Councillor of the Henan branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至則修城池，飭備禦，賊不敢犯其境。

translations.literal: When he arrived he repaired walls and moats and tightened defenses; the bandits dared not encroach on his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he repaired the walls and tightened defenses, and the bandits dared not enter his territory.

sentences.zh: 遷淮南行省平章政事。

translations.literal: Transferred to Grand Councillor of the Huainan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Councillor of the Huainan branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十五年，入為中書平章政事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he entered service as Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he entered the capital as Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時中書庶務多為吏胥遲留，至則責委提控掾史二人分督左右曹，悉為剖決。

translations.literal: At the time many routine affairs of the Central Secretariat were delayed and held up by clerks and underlings; when he arrived he assigned two supervising secretaries to oversee the left and right offices in turn, and all were adjudicated.
translations.idiomatic: Routine business at the Central Secretariat was then often delayed by clerks. On taking office he put two supervising secretaries in charge of the left and right offices and had every case decided.

sentences.zh: 出為江浙行省左丞相，尋兼知行樞密院事，許以便宜行事。

translations.literal: He went out as Left Councillor of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat; soon he also concurrently directed Privy Council affairs and was permitted discretionary action.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as Left Councillor of the Jiangzhe branch secretariat, soon also given concurrent charge of Privy Council affairs, with permission to act at discretion.

sentences.zh: 時江淮盜勢日盛，南北阻隔。

translations.literal: At the time bandit strength on the Yangzi and Huai grew daily; north and south were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit power along the Yangzi and Huai grew daily, and north and south were cut off from one another.

sentences.zh: 達識帖睦邇獨治方面，而任用非人，肆通賄賂，賣官鬻爵，一視貨之輕重以為高下，於是謗議紛然。

translations.literal: Dashitiemuer alone governed the region, yet he employed unworthy men, freely traded bribes, sold offices and bartered ranks — viewing goods' weight and lightness to determine high and low — and thus criticism arose everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Dashitiemuer alone governed the region, yet he put unworthy men in office, took bribes openly, and sold offices and ranks according to the price offered, until criticism swirled everywhere.

sentences.zh: 所部郡縣往往淪陷，亦恬不以為意。

translations.literal: Commanderies and districts under his jurisdiction often fell, yet he remained untroubled and took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: Commanderies and districts under his jurisdiction often fell, yet he remained untroubled and took no notice.

sentences.zh: 十六年正月，張士誠陷平江。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixteenth year, Zhang Shicheng captured Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixteenth year Zhang Shicheng captured Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 七月，逼杭州，達識帖睦邇即棄城遁於富陽。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, pressing Hangzhou, Dashitiemuer immediately abandoned the city and fled to Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, as Zhang Shicheng pressed Hangzhou, Dashitiemuer abandoned the city and fled to Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 萬戶普賢奴力拒之，而苗軍帥楊完者時駐嘉興，亦引兵至，敗走張士誠，達識帖睦邇乃還。

translations.literal: Wanhu Pu Huatieer resisted him with force; meanwhile Yang Waner, commander of the Miao army, was stationed at Jiaxing and also led troops there, defeated and drove off Zhang Shicheng, and Dashitiemuer then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wanhu Pu Huatieer resisted him fiercely. Yang Waner, commander of the Miao army, was then stationed at Jiaxing and also brought troops up; together they defeated Zhang Shicheng and drove him off, and Dashitiemuer returned.

sentences.zh: 初，達識帖睦邇以完者為海北宣慰使都元帥，尋升江浙行省參政，至是遂升右丞。

translations.literal: Initially Dashitiemuer had made Waner Military Pacification Commissioner and Commander-in-Chief of Haibei; soon promoted him to associate chief minister of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat; at this juncture he was then promoted to right vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Dashitiemuer had made Waner Pacification Commissioner and Commander-in-Chief of Haibei, then promoted him to associate chief minister of the Jiangzhe branch secretariat; now he was raised to right vice director.

sentences.zh: 而苗軍素無紀律，肆為鈔掠，所過蕩然無遺。

translations.literal: But the Miao army had always lacked discipline and freely plundered; wherever they passed nothing remained.
translations.idiomatic: But the Miao army had never known discipline and plundered wherever they went, leaving nothing behind.

sentences.zh: 達識帖睦邇方倚完者以為重，莫敢禁遏，故完者矜驕日肆而不可製。

translations.literal: Dashitiemuer was just then relying on Waner as his mainstay and dared not restrain him; thus Waner grew ever more arrogant and unchecked, beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: Dashitiemuer was then relying on Waner as his main strength and dared not restrain him, so Waner grew ever more arrogant and beyond control.

sentences.zh: 明年，士誠寇嘉興，屢為完者所敗。

translations.literal: The next year Shicheng raided Jiaxing and was repeatedly defeated by Waner.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Shicheng attacked Jiaxing and was repeatedly defeated by Waner.

sentences.zh: 士誠乃遣蠻子海牙以書詐降。

translations.literal: Shicheng then sent Manzi Haiya with a letter feigning surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng then sent Manzi Haiya with a letter offering a false surrender.

sentences.zh: 蠻子海牙嘗為南行台御史中丞，以軍結水寨，屯採石，為大明兵所敗，因走歸士誠，故士誠使之來。

translations.literal: Manzi Haiya had once been vice censor-in-chief of the Southern Branch Censorate; he gathered troops and built a water fort, encamped at Caishi, was defeated by the Ming army, and thus fled back to Shicheng — therefore Shicheng sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Manzi Haiya had once been vice censor-in-chief of the Southern Branch Censorate. He had gathered troops into a water fort at Caishi, been defeated by the Ming army, and fled back to Shicheng — which was why Shicheng now sent him.

sentences.zh: 而書詞多不遜。

translations.literal: But the letter's wording was largely impertinent.
translations.idiomatic: But the letter's language was largely impertinent.

sentences.zh: 完者欲納之，達識帖睦邇不可，曰：「我昔在淮南，嘗招安士誠，知其反覆，其降不可信。」

translations.literal: Waner wished to accept it; Dashitiemuer would not permit it, saying: "I was once in Huainan and tried to win Shicheng over; I know his fickleness — his surrender cannot be trusted."
translations.idiomatic: Waner wanted to accept the offer. Dashitiemuer refused, saying, "When I was in Huainan I once tried to win Shicheng over. I know how fickle he is — his surrender cannot be trusted."

sentences.zh: 完者固勸，乃許之。

translations.literal: Waner firmly urged, and so it was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Waner pressed hard, and in the end it was allowed.

sentences.zh: 士誠始要王爵，達識帖睦邇不許。

translations.literal: Shicheng at first demanded a princely title; Dashitiemuer would not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shicheng demanded a princely title, and Dashitiemuer refused.

sentences.zh: 又請爵為三公，達識帖睦邇曰：「三公非有司所定，今我雖便宜行事，然不敢專也。」

translations.literal: He then requested rank as one of the Three Excellencies; Dashitiemuer said: "The Three Excellencies are not for a subordinate office to determine; though I may now act at discretion, I dare not decide alone."
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to be made one of the Three Excellencies. Dashitiemuer said, "The Three Excellencies are not for a local officer to appoint. Though I may act at discretion, I dare not decide this alone."

sentences.zh: 完者又力以為請，達識帖睦邇雖外為正詞，然實幸其降，又恐忤完者意，遂授士誠太尉，其弟士德淮南行省平章政事，士信同知行樞密院事，其黨皆授官有差。

translations.literal: Waner again vigorously pleaded on his behalf; although outwardly Dashitiemuer spoke upright words, in truth he hoped for the surrender and also feared offending Waner's wishes; he then bestowed on Shicheng the title Grand Commandant, his brother Shide Grand Councillor of the Huainan Branch Secretariat, Shixin associate administrator of the Privy Council, and his followers all received offices according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Waner again pressed the request hard. Outwardly Dashitiemuer spoke uprightly, but in truth he hoped for the surrender and feared offending Waner; he therefore made Shicheng Grand Commandant, his brother Shide Grand Councillor of the Huainan branch secretariat, Shixin associate administrator of the Privy Council, and gave offices of varying rank to his followers.

sentences.zh: 士德尋為大明兵所擒。

translations.literal: Shide was soon captured by the Ming army.
translations.idiomatic: Shide was soon captured by the Ming army.

sentences.zh: 复升士信淮南行省平章政事。

translations.literal: Shixin was again promoted to Grand Councillor of the Huainan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shixin was then promoted to Grand Councillor of the Huainan branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 然士誠雖降，而城池府庫甲兵錢穀皆自據如故。

translations.literal: Yet though Shicheng had surrendered, cities, treasuries, armor, weapons, money, and grain he still held as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though Shicheng had submitted, he still held cities, treasuries, arms, and grain as before.

sentences.zh: 於是朝廷以招安張士誠為達識帖木兒功，詔加太尉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the court regarded winning Zhang Shicheng over as Dashitiemuer's achievement and issued an edict adding the title Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The court then counted the winning over of Zhang Shicheng as Dashitiemuer's achievement and issued an edict promoting him to Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 當是時，徽州、建德皆已陷，完者屢出師不利。

translations.literal: At that time Huizhou and Jiande had both fallen; Waner repeatedly took the field without success.
translations.idiomatic: By then Huizhou and Jiande had both fallen, and Waner repeatedly took the field without success.

sentences.zh: 士誠素欲圖完者，而完者時又強娶平章政事慶童女，達識帖木兒雖主其婚，然亦甚厭之，乃陰與士誠定計除完者。

translations.literal: Shicheng had long wished to eliminate Waner; meanwhile Waner had forcibly taken in marriage the daughter of Grand Councillor Qing Tong; although Dashitiemuer had arranged the marriage, he too greatly detested it — and thus secretly joined Shicheng in a plot to remove Waner.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng had long wanted to destroy Waner. Waner had also forcibly taken Grand Councillor Qing Tong's daughter in marriage. Dashitiemuer had arranged the match, yet he too loathed Waner deeply, and so secretly plotted with Shicheng to remove him.

sentences.zh: 揚言使士誠出兵復建德，完者營在杭城北，不為備，遂被圍，苗軍悉潰，完者與其弟伯顏皆自殺。

translations.literal: They spread word that Shicheng's troops would march out to recover Jiande; Waner's camp was north of Hangzhou city and made no preparations; he was then besieged, the Miao army all routed; Waner and his younger brother Bayan both killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They spread word that Shicheng would send troops to recover Jiande. Waner's camp lay north of Hangzhou and was unprepared; he was surrounded, the Miao army routed, and Waner and his brother Bayan both killed themselves.

sentences.zh: 其後事聞於朝，贈完者潭國忠愍公，伯顏衡國忠烈公。

translations.literal: Afterward when the matter reached the court, Waner was posthumously granted Duke Zhongmin of Tan, and Bayan Duke Zhonglie of Heng.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Waner was posthumously made Duke Zhongmin of Tan and Bayan Duke Zhonglie of Heng.

sentences.zh: 完者既死，士誠兵遂據杭州。

translations.literal: Once Waner was dead, Shicheng's troops then occupied Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once Waner was dead, Shicheng's troops occupied Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十九年，朝廷因授士信江浙行省平章政事。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, the court accordingly appointed Shixin Grand Councillor of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the court appointed Shixin Grand Councillor of the Jiangzhe branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 士信乃大發浙西諸郡民築杭城。

translations.literal: Shixin then massively conscripted the people of the western Zhe circuits to build Hangzhou's walls.
translations.idiomatic: Shixin then conscripted the people of western Zhe on a great scale to build Hangzhou's walls.

sentences.zh: 先是，海漕久不通，朝廷遣使來徵糧，士誠運米十餘萬石達京師。

translations.literal: Earlier, sea transport had long been cut off; the court sent envoys to levy grain; Shicheng shipped more than a hundred thousand shi of rice to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Sea transport had long been cut off. The court sent envoys to levy grain, and Shicheng shipped more than a hundred thousand shi of rice to the capital.

sentences.zh: 方面之權，悉歸張氏，達識帖睦邇徒存虛名而已。

translations.literal: Regional authority all passed to the Zhang clan; Dashitiemuer retained only an empty name.
translations.idiomatic: Regional power passed entirely to the Zhang clan, and Dashitiemuer retained only an empty title.

sentences.zh: 俄而士誠令其部屬自頌功德，必欲求王爵。

translations.literal: Before long Shicheng ordered his subordinates to praise their own merits and necessarily sought a princely title.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shicheng had his subordinates praise his merits and insist on a princely title.

sentences.zh: 達識帖睦邇謂左右曰：「我承製居此，徒籍口舌以馭此輩。

translations.literal: Dashitiemuer said to those beside him: "I hold this post by imperial commission and govern these men by words alone.
translations.idiomatic: Dashitiemuer said to those around him, "I hold this post by imperial commission and govern these men by words alone.

sentences.zh: 今張氏复要王爵，朝廷雖微，終不為其所脅，但我今若逆其意，則目前必受害，當忍恥含垢以從之耳。」

translations.literal: Now the Zhangs again demand a princely title; though the court has waned, it will in the end not be coerced by them — but if I now go against their will, I will certainly suffer harm in the present; I must bear shame and swallow disgrace to comply."
translations.idiomatic: Now the Zhangs again demand a princely title. The court may be weak, but it will not in the end be coerced by them — yet if I oppose them now, I will surely come to harm. I must bear shame and swallow disgrace and go along."

sentences.zh: 乃為具文書聞於朝，至再三，不報。

translations.literal: He then prepared documents reporting to the court; again and again he did so, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: He then drew up documents reporting to the court, again and again, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 士誠遂自立為吳王，即平江治宮闕，立官屬。

translations.literal: Shicheng then declared himself Prince of Wu, established palace halls at Pingjiang, and appointed officials.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng then declared himself Prince of Wu, built palace halls at Pingjiang, and appointed officials.

sentences.zh: 時答蘭帖木兒為江浙行省右丞，真保為左右司郎中，二人諂事士誠，多受金帛，數媒孽達識帖睦邇之短，以故張氏遂有不相容之勢。

translations.literal: At the time Dalantemuer was right vice director of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat and Zhenbao was director in the left and right offices; the two flattered and served Shicheng, received much gold and silk, and repeatedly slandered Dashitiemuer's faults — hence the Zhang clan came to have an incompatible rivalry with him.
translations.idiomatic: Dalantemuer was then right vice director of the Jiangzhe branch secretariat and Zhenbao director in the left and right offices. The two fawned on Shicheng, took much gold and silk, and repeatedly spoke ill of Dashitiemuer, so the Zhang clan came to be at odds with him.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，士信乃使王晟等面數達識帖睦邇過失，勒其移諮省院，自陳老病願退。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Shixin sent Wang Sheng and others to enumerate Dashitiemuer's faults to his face and compel him to transfer his petition to the branch secretariat and central offices, declaring himself aged and ill and wishing to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year Shixin sent Wang Sheng and others to recite Dashitiemuer's faults to his face and force him to submit a petition to the branch secretariat and central offices declaring himself aged and ill and wishing to retire.

sentences.zh: 又言：「丞相之任非士信不可。」

translations.literal: They also said: "The post of chief councillor can be held by none but Shixin."
translations.idiomatic: They also said, "The post of chief councillor can be held by none but Shixin."

sentences.zh: 士信即逼取其諸所掌符印，而自為江浙行省左丞相，徙達識帖睦邇居嘉興。

translations.literal: Shixin immediately seized all the seals and tallies in his charge and installed himself as Left Councillor of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat, moving Dashitiemuer to reside at Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shixin immediately seized all the seals and tallies in his charge, made himself Left Councillor of the Jiangzhe branch secretariat, and moved Dashitiemuer to Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 事聞朝廷，即就以士信為江浙行省左丞相。

translations.literal: When the matter reached the court, Shixin was immediately appointed Left Councillor of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Shixin was at once appointed Left Councillor of the Jiangzhe branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 達識帖睦邇至嘉興，士信峻其垣牆，錮其門闥，所以防禁之者甚嚴。

translations.literal: When Dashitiemuer arrived at Jiaxing, Shixin heightened his walls, barred his gates and doors — the measures to guard and confine him were very strict.
translations.idiomatic: When Dashitiemuer reached Jiaxing, Shixin raised his walls, barred his gates, and guarded him with the strictest confinement.

sentences.zh: 達識帖睦邇皆不以為意，日對妻妾飲酒放歌自若。

translations.literal: Dashitiemuer paid none of it any mind and daily drank and sang freely before his wives and concubines as before.
translations.idiomatic: Dashitiemuer paid no heed and daily drank and sang freely with his wives and concubines as before.

sentences.zh: 士誠令有司公牘皆首稱「吳王令旨」，又諷行台為請實授於朝，行台御史大夫普化帖木兒皆不從。

translations.literal: Shicheng ordered all government documents to begin with "By order of the Prince of Wu"; he also prompted the Branch Secretariat to request formal appointment from the court — Branch Censor-in-Chief Puhua Timur would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng ordered all government documents to begin with "By order of the Prince of Wu" and also prompted the branch censorate to request formal appointment from the court, but Branch Censor-in-Chief Puhua Timur refused.

sentences.zh: 至是，既拘達識帖睦邇，即使人至紹興從普化帖木兒索行台印章。

translations.literal: At this point, having already confined Dashitiemuer, he sent men to Shaoxing to demand the Branch Secretariat seals from Puhua Timur.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Dashitiemuer was confined, he sent men to Shaoxing to demand the branch censorate seals from Puhua Timur.

sentences.zh: 普化帖木兒封其印置諸庫，曰：「我頭可斷，印不可與。」

translations.literal: Puhua Timur sealed the seals and placed them in the treasury, saying: "My head may be cut off — the seal may not be given."
translations.idiomatic: Puhua Timur sealed the seals and put them in the treasury, saying, "My head may be cut off, but the seal will not be given."

sentences.zh: 又迫之登舟，曰：「​​我可死，不可辱也。」

translations.literal: They again forced him to board a boat; he said: "I can die — I cannot be shamed."
translations.idiomatic: They again forced him aboard a boat. He said, "I can die, but I cannot be shamed."

sentences.zh: 從容沐浴更衣，與妻子訣，賦詩二章，乃仰藥而死。

translations.literal: He calmly bathed and changed clothes, took leave of wife and children, composed two poems, and then swallowed poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: He bathed calmly, changed his clothes, took leave of wife and children, composed two poems, and swallowed poison and died.

sentences.zh: 臨死，擲杯地上曰：「我死矣，逆賊當踵我亡也。」

translations.literal: At the point of death he cast a cup to the ground, saying: "I am dead — the rebel traitors shall follow me to extinction."
translations.idiomatic: At the point of death he cast a cup to the ground and said, "I am dead — the rebel traitors will follow me to ruin."

sentences.zh: 後數日，達識帖睦邇聞之，歎曰：「大夫且死，吾不死何為！」

translations.literal: Several days later Dashitiemuer heard of it and sighed: "The grand minister is about to die — why should I not die!"
translations.idiomatic: Several days later Dashitiemuer heard of it and sighed, "The grand minister is about to die — why should I not die!"

sentences.zh: 遂命左右以藥酒進，飲之而死。

translations.literal: He then ordered those beside him to bring medicinal wine; he drank it and died.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered his attendants to bring medicinal wine, drank it, and died.

sentences.zh: 士誠乃使載其柩及妻孥北返於京師。

translations.literal: Shicheng then had his coffin and wife and children carried north back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng then had his coffin and wife and children sent north to the capital.

sentences.zh: 普化帖木兒字兼善，答魯乃蠻氏，行台御史大夫帖木哥子也。

translations.literal: Puhua Timur, courtesy name Jianshan, was of the Qarlughas clan; he was the son of Branch Censor-in-Chief Temuge.
translations.idiomatic: Puhua Timur, styled Jianshan, was of the Qarlughas clan and the son of Branch Censor-in-Chief Temuge.

sentences.zh: 累遷福建行省平章政事，時境內皆為諸豪所據，不能有所施設。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Councillor of the Fujian Branch Secretariat; at the time the territory within was all held by various powerful chiefs, and he could accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Councillor of the Fujian branch secretariat, but the province was then held by local strongmen and he could accomplish nothing.

sentences.zh: 及遷南行台，又​​為張士誠所逼而死。

translations.literal: When transferred to the Southern Branch Secretariat, he was again forced by Zhang Shicheng to his death.
translations.idiomatic: When he was transferred to the Southern Branch Censorate, Zhang Shicheng again forced him to his death.

sentences.zh: 然論者以為其死視達識帖睦邇為差勝云。

translations.literal: Yet commentators held that his death, compared with Dashitiemuer's, was somewhat the better.
translations.idiomatic: Yet commentators held that compared with Dashitiemuer, his death was somewhat the more honorable.
